_about: Deliberate changes to the call contract of tools that are on master. Each entry needs a real benefit and what a caller must change. tests/test_backward_compat.py fails on any undeclared change, and on any entry here that no longer matches a detected change. Kinds: removed_tool, removed_parameter, new_required_parameter, default_changed (all detected automatically), and behaviour (a change the signature does not show, such as stricter validation or a changed response field; not detected, so declare it by hand). A behaviour entry may use tool "*" when the change applies to every tool on master.

changes.what_changed: An id that contains a slash, a question mark, a hash, two dots in a row or a space is now refused before any request is sent. Before, such an id was placed in the request address as written, so get_creative('123/') read creative 123 and an id like '123/ads' read a different object than the tool was meant to read.
changes.why_better: A tool can only reach the object type it was built for. An id copied from text that strangers wrote (an ad comment, a Page review) can no longer steer a read or a delete to a different object or attach extra options to the request.
changes.migration: Pass the plain id with nothing before or after it, for example '123' or 'act_123'. Trim a trailing slash or any address fragment before calling.

changes.what_changed: file_path is now read only from the one folder named by the META_UPLOAD_DIR environment variable, the same rule every other upload tool follows. A path outside that folder, a link inside it that points outside, a file that is not .jpg, .jpeg or .png, an empty file and a file over 30 MB are refused before anything is sent to Meta, and every local path is refused while META_UPLOAD_DIR is unset. Before, any file anywhere on the machine was read and sent to Meta, whatever its type or size. The request sent for an accepted file is unchanged, and image_url calls are unchanged.
changes.why_better: The model that calls this tool also reads text written by strangers, such as ad comments and Page reviews. Before, a path slipped into that text could make the tool send any private file on your computer, such as a key or a document, to a Meta ad account. Now only images you have put in your chosen upload folder can ever leave the machine, and a wrong path gets a clear message that never repeats the path.
changes.migration: Set META_UPLOAD_DIR in the server's environment to one folder, put the images to upload there, and pass a path inside that folder or a file name relative to it. Use .jpg, .jpeg or .png files of at most 30 MB. Calls that pass image_url need no change.

changes.what_changed: spend_cap inside params is now refused before any request is sent, with a message pointing to the named spend_cap parameter. Before, params={'spend_cap': 25000} was sent to Meta as written and read in minor units (250.00 USD), while the named spend_cap takes major units (spend_cap=250 is 250.00). daily_budget and lifetime_budget inside params were already refused; only their message changed.
changes.why_better: The same field no longer has two units, so an amount cannot silently be 100 times too small (or too large) because it was put in params instead of the named parameter.
changes.migration: Move the amount to the named spend_cap parameter in major units: divide the minor-unit amount you sent in params by the currency's minor-unit factor, 100 for most currencies and 1 for currencies without minor units such as JPY or KRW. params={'spend_cap': 25000} in USD becomes spend_cap=250.

changes.what_changed: spend_cap inside params is now refused before any request is sent, including the read of the campaign, with a message pointing to the named spend_cap parameter. Before, params={'spend_cap': 25000} was sent to Meta as written and read in minor units (250.00 USD), while the named spend_cap takes major units. daily_budget and lifetime_budget inside params were already refused; only their message changed.
changes.why_better: The same field no longer has two units, so an amount cannot silently be 100 times too small (or too large) because it was put in params instead of the named parameter.
changes.migration: Move the amount to the named spend_cap parameter in major units: divide the minor-unit amount you sent in params by the currency's minor-unit factor, 100 for most currencies and 1 for currencies without minor units such as JPY or KRW. params={'spend_cap': 25000} in USD becomes spend_cap=250.

changes.what_changed: daily_spend_cap, lifetime_spend_cap, daily_min_spend_target and lifetime_min_spend_target inside params are now refused before any request is sent, with a message pointing to the named parameter of the same name. Before, they were sent to Meta as written and read in minor units, while the named parameters take major units. bid_amount, daily_budget and lifetime_budget inside params were already refused; only their message changed.
changes.why_better: The same field no longer has two units, so an amount cannot silently be 100 times too small (or too large) because it was put in params instead of the named parameter.
changes.migration: Move each amount to the named parameter of the same name in major units: divide the minor-unit amount you sent in params by the currency's minor-unit factor, 100 for most currencies and 1 for currencies without minor units such as JPY or KRW. params={'daily_spend_cap': 9000} in USD becomes daily_spend_cap=90.

changes.what_changed: When a call changes the audience rule, whether through the named rule parameter or through params={'rule': ...}, the tool now also asks Meta for the audience's current rule in the read it already makes before updating, and returns it as previous.rule. Before, a params-only rule change read and returned the other fields but not the old rule.
changes.why_better: The rule decides who is in the audience, and Meta does not keep the old one. Returning it before it is replaced is the only way to put it back if the new rule turns out to be wrong.
changes.migration: No change to how the tool is called. The response has one more field, previous.rule; the read before the update asks for one more field.

changes.what_changed: When start_time or end_time is given without a time zone (for example 2026-11-27T00:00:00), the ad set is still created with exactly the same request as before, but the tool then reads the new ad set once and the response gains two fields: warnings, saying the time had no time zone so Meta chose how to read it, and stored_schedule, the start and end time Meta stored. With validate_only the warning is given without the read. A time with an offset, Unix seconds or no time at all makes the same requests and returns the same fields as before.
changes.why_better: A time with no time zone can be read as a different hour than the caller meant, which starts or ends delivery hours early or late. Showing what Meta stored makes a shift visible at once, without refusing calls that worked before.
changes.migration: No change to how the tool is called. To avoid the warning and the extra read, pass times with a UTC offset, for example 2026-11-27T00:00:00-05:00. If the read after the create fails, the create is still reported as a success with its id.

changes.what_changed: A campaign created without a campaign budget (no daily_budget and no lifetime_budget) and without is_adset_budget_sharing_enabled, named or inside params, is now sent with is_adset_budget_sharing_enabled false, one more field than before, and the response gains defaults_applied naming the field, the value sent and why. This applies to validate_only calls too. A campaign with a campaign budget is sent exactly as before, and a caller who gives the field gets exactly the value given.
changes.why_better: Meta now refuses every campaign without a campaign budget unless this choice is sent (seen live on 2026-11-13: code 100, subcode 4834011), so the old call always failed. It now succeeds, with each ad set keeping its own budget, which is how such campaigns behaved before Meta added budget sharing, and the response says what was chosen.
changes.migration: Nothing to change. To let ad sets share up to 20 percent of their budgets, pass is_adset_budget_sharing_enabled=true; to state the default yourself, pass false.

changes.what_changed: When start_time or stop_time is sent, named or inside params, a real create (not validate_only) now reads the new campaign's start_time and stop_time once after the create, and the response gains stored_schedule (what Meta holds; a start Meta reports as 1969 or 1970, meaning unset, is shown as null) and, when a sent time was not stored, warnings saying so. The create request itself is unchanged. If the read fails, the create is still reported as a success, with a warning that the stored times could not be read.
changes.why_better: Meta accepts a campaign's start_time and stop_time and stores neither (seen live on 2026-11-13): a campaign's schedule comes from its ad sets. Before, the caller had no sign that the times were ignored and could believe the campaign was scheduled when it was not.
changes.migration: No change to how the tool is called. Set start and end times on the ad sets (create_ad_set or update_adset) instead of the campaign; a call without start_time or stop_time makes the same requests and returns the same fields as before.

changes.what_changed: When start_time or stop_time is sent, named or inside params, the tool now reads the campaign's start_time and stop_time once after the update and adds stored_schedule to the response. A sent time that Meta did not store is no longer listed under current; it moves to a new field, sent, and warnings says Meta did not store it. A sent time Meta did store stays in current, and every other field of current is unchanged. If the read fails, the update is still reported as a success, the times are listed under sent, and a warning says the stored times could not be read.
changes.why_better: Meta accepts a campaign's start_time and stop_time and stores neither (seen live on 2026-11-13), and the tool used to report the times it sent as the campaign's current values, which was false. The response now shows what the campaign really holds.
changes.migration: Read the times you sent from sent instead of current when Meta did not store them, and read what Meta holds from stored_schedule. Set schedules on the ad sets (update_adset) instead of the campaign. A call without start_time or stop_time makes the same requests and returns the same fields as before.

changes.what_changed: When Meta answers with a success status but the body cannot be read as a JSON object (it is not JSON, or it is a bare null, text or number), the tool now raises a Meta API error saying the answer could not be read. After a write the error says the outcome is not known. Before, a body that was not JSON was handed to the tool as an object, so a write was reported as done and a tool that reads before it writes went on to write; a bare null or number crashed the tool.
changes.why_better: An answer that cannot be read is no longer presented as a result. A caller is told plainly that a write may or may not have happened, and no tool acts on a read it could not read.
changes.migration: Nothing to change for a normal answer. Where a caller handled this case, treat the error like any other Meta error; when it says the outcome is not known, read the object before retrying.

changes.what_changed: When Meta's answer to the image read has no list of images, or holds an entry that cannot be read, the tool now raises the same error it already raised when more images existed than it read: it could not obtain a complete image result. Before, an answer with no list was returned as a complete result with the images marked unresolved, and an unreadable entry crashed the tool.
changes.why_better: A result is no longer called complete when the read behind it could not be read.
changes.migration: Nothing to change. This only happens when Meta's answer is malformed; treat the error like any other failed read.

changes.what_changed: When Meta answers a page of audiences without a readable data list (data missing, null or not a list), the tool now returns no items with summary.complete false, summary.next_after null and summary.incomplete_reason saying the page could not be read. Before, a missing data list was returned as an empty, complete list, a null data list crashed the tool, and a data value that was not a list was returned as the items. A page that holds an entry that is not an object (for example null) still shows its items as Meta returned them, but summary.complete is now false with summary.incomplete_reason saying how many entries could not be read; summary.next_after is kept when Meta reported a next page. Before, such a page was called complete. A normal page, including an empty data list, returns exactly what it did before.
changes.why_better: A page that could not be read, or that holds an entry that could not be read, is no longer presented as proof that the account has no more audiences, so a caller does not stop paging, or conclude an audience does not exist, on an answer that said nothing.
changes.migration: Nothing to change for a normal answer. A caller that pages until complete is true should also stop when next_after is null, and treat complete false with incomplete_reason as a list that was not fully read: retry the call or report it.

changes.what_changed: When Meta answers a page of ad accounts that cannot be read in full, the result now says so: summary.complete is false and summary.incomplete_reason gives the reason. A page with no data list (data missing, null or not a list) returns no items and no paging cursor. A page with entries that are not objects returns the accounts that were read, without those entries, and Meta's paging. Before, a missing data list was returned as an ordinary empty last page, and a null data list or an entry that was not an object crashed the tool. A normal page, including an empty one, returns exactly what it did before, with no complete key.
changes.why_better: An answer from Meta that could not be read is no longer shown as proof that the token can see no ad accounts, or no more of them, so a caller does not stop looking on an answer that said nothing.
changes.migration: Nothing to change for a normal answer. A caller should treat summary.complete false with summary.incomplete_reason as a list that was not fully read: retry the call or report it.

changes.what_changed: When Meta answers a write (a POST or DELETE) with a success status and an explicit false (a bare false, or an object whose success field is false), the tool now raises a Meta API error saying Meta answered that the change was not made. Before, that answer was handed to the tool as a result, and write tools reported the change as made. Only the boolean false counts: an answer with no success field, or with success true, is returned exactly as before, and reads are not affected.
changes.why_better: A change Meta says it did not make is no longer reported as made.
changes.migration: Nothing to change for a normal answer. Treat the error like any other Meta error: read the object to see what it holds before retrying.

changes.what_changed: When Meta answers a write (a POST or DELETE) with a success status whose body is a throttling error, the rate-limit error the tool raises now says the outcome is not known: retryable is false, and mutation_outcome_unknown true and next_step are added. Before, it said retryable true, as for an ordinary throttle. A throttling error on an error status (the ordinary case) is unchanged: retryable true, with no added field.
changes.why_better: A success status with an error body contradicts itself, so the change may have been made; the caller is told to check before retrying instead of being told a retry is safe.
changes.migration: Nothing to change for an ordinary throttle. When a rate-limit error carries mutation_outcome_unknown true, read the object before retrying.

changes.what_changed: Two answers to a write (a POST or DELETE) are now reported as an unknown outcome. First, an answer that holds success true together with an error or an error status: the error the tool raises now has mutation_outcome_unknown true and retryable false; before, it was reported as a plain refusal. This holds whichever error it is: a rate-limit error keeps its type; an answer that would have been reported as an unsupported feature or as not found is raised as a Meta API error instead, so it can carry the flag. The same holds for a write answered as unsupported or not found whose error Meta marks transient: it is raised as a Meta API error with mutation_outcome_unknown true. Second, an answer nested too deeply to decode: the tool raises the same error as for a body that is not JSON (change 11); before, the decoder's own error escaped. An ordinary error answer, with no success true beside it, is unchanged, and reads are unchanged.
changes.why_better: An answer that says both that the change succeeded and that it failed does not show the change was refused, so the caller is told to check before retrying.
changes.migration: Nothing to change for a normal answer. When an error carries mutation_outcome_unknown true, read the object before retrying.

changes.what_changed: Money is converted by the offset Meta documents for each currency. For ad accounts in COP, CRC, HUF, IDR or TWD, Meta's offset is 1 (amounts are whole units), and every budget, bid, spend cap and minimum spend is now sent and read as whole units. Before, these five were treated like a two-decimal currency: an amount was multiplied by 100 on the way to Meta, so a daily budget of 500 was sent as 50000, and divided by 100 when read. An amount with a fraction is now refused for these five. Ad accounts in BGN, BHD, JOD, RSD, RUB, VES and the other currencies Meta lists are now accepted, at Meta's offset of 100; before, money tools refused them as unsupported. Every other currency, including USD, EUR and JPY, converts exactly as before.
changes.why_better: Budgets and bids for accounts in these five currencies were sent 100 times larger than the caller asked for and read back 100 times smaller.
changes.migration: Nothing to change for other currencies. For an account in COP, CRC, HUF, IDR or TWD: pass the real amount (500 means 500). A caller that divided inputs by 100, or multiplied outputs by 100, to work around the old conversion must stop doing so.

changes.what_changed: With include_creative_summary=true, creative fields the caller names in fields (for example creative{image_hash}) are now merged into the creative selection instead of being replaced by the summary fields, so the request asks for and the result returns those fields as well. A call without an explicit creative{...} selection sends exactly the request it sent before.
changes.why_better: The option no longer silently drops creative fields the caller asked for.
changes.migration: None. A caller who relied on the summary alone can leave the creative{...} selection out of fields.

changes.what_changed: When Meta answers the read of one object with a success status and a bare true, false or array where an object belongs, the tool now raises a Meta API error saying the answer could not be read. Before, that answer was handed to the tool as an object with no fields: a tool that reads an object before changing it went on to write and reported every previous value as absent, and a read reported the object as found with nothing set. Any JSON object, including an empty one, is returned exactly as before; list reads and writes are not affected.
changes.why_better: An answer that is not the object asked for is no longer read as an object with nothing set, so no tool writes on a before-state it never read.
changes.migration: Nothing to change for a normal answer. Treat the error like any other failed read.

changes.what_changed: search_behaviors now reads Meta's list of behavior categories (the search route with type adTargetingCategory and class behaviors) and keeps the rows whose name contains query, ignoring case; no query keeps every row. Before, it read the ad account's broadtargetingcategories edge, which lists only that account's custom categories, so it returned an empty list for every query with no error. Rows now carry the fields Meta's search route returns, as Meta returns them. The summary adds rows_read, rows_matched, pages_read, complete, truncated and next_after, and a note when nothing matched. paging.next is now always null. account_id is no longer needed. A limit below 1 is refused.
changes.why_better: The tool returns Meta's real behavior categories instead of an empty list, and an empty result now says whether Meta sent rows that did not match the query or sent nothing at all.
changes.migration: Read id and name from each row as before. To get more rows, call again with after=summary.next_after until summary.complete is true; if summary.incomplete_reason says matches were cut by limit, raise limit.

changes.what_changed: search_demographics now reads Meta's list of categories of demographic_class (the search route with type adTargetingCategory and that class) and keeps the rows whose name contains query, ignoring case; no query keeps every row. Before, it read the ad account's broadtargetingcategories edge, which lists only that account's custom categories, so it returned an empty list for every query with no error. Rows now carry the fields Meta's search route returns, as Meta returns them. The summary adds rows_read, rows_matched, pages_read, complete, truncated and next_after, and a note when nothing matched. paging.next is now always null. account_id is no longer needed. A limit below 1 is refused.
changes.why_better: The tool returns Meta's real demographic categories instead of an empty list, and an empty result now says whether Meta sent rows that did not match the query or sent nothing at all.
changes.migration: Read id and name from each row as before. To get more rows, call again with after=summary.next_after until summary.complete is true; if summary.incomplete_reason says matches were cut by limit, raise limit.

changes.what_changed: get_targeting_categories now reads Meta's list of categories of category_class (the search route with type adTargetingCategory and that class) and keeps the rows whose name contains query, ignoring case; no query keeps every row. Before, it read the ad account's broadtargetingcategories edge, which lists only that account's custom categories, so it returned an empty list for every class with no error. Rows now carry the fields Meta's search route returns, as Meta returns them. The summary adds rows_read, rows_matched, pages_read, complete, truncated and next_after, and a note when nothing matched. paging.next is now always null. account_id is no longer needed. A limit below 1 is refused.
changes.why_better: The tool returns Meta's real targeting categories instead of an empty list, and an empty result now says whether Meta sent rows that did not match the query or sent nothing for that class.
changes.migration: Read id and name from each row as before. To get more rows, call again with after=summary.next_after until summary.complete is true; if summary.incomplete_reason says matches were cut by limit, raise limit.

changes.what_changed: Before, the type filter was ignored: subtype was sent as a parameter Meta does not read, so every audience came back whatever type was asked for. Now Meta is asked to filter (a filtering clause on subtype, the value upper-cased) and returns only audiences of that type, still one request per call with limit and after working as without subtype. The tool also always reads the subtype field (removing it from the rows again when fields leaves it out) and drops any row of another type or without a type, ignoring case; when it drops a row, summary.complete is false and summary.incomplete_reason says how many were dropped. The summary adds rows_read and rows_matched. A blank subtype counts as none. Calls without subtype are unchanged.
changes.why_better: Asking for lookalike audiences now returns only lookalike audiences, in one request. Before, the caller got every kind of audience back and could take a custom audience for a lookalike one.
changes.migration: Nothing to change to get the filtered list. If summary.incomplete_reason says rows of another type were dropped, Meta may not have applied the filter: keep paging with after=summary.next_after, or report it.

changes.what_changed: spend_cap, when named in fields, is now returned in major units of the account currency, like amount_spent and balance: a cap of 250.00 USD comes back as 250.0, not 25000. For a currency with no minor unit, such as JPY, the number is unchanged. A spend_cap of 0 still comes back as 0.
changes.why_better: The tool's description already said amounts are in major units, so a spend cap read 100 times too large could be mistaken for a much higher limit. update_campaign also shows spend_cap in major units, so reads and writes now use the same scale.
changes.migration: If you divided spend_cap by 100 (or by the currency's minor-unit factor) yourself, stop: use the value as returned.

changes.what_changed: spend_cap, when named in fields, is now returned in major units of the account currency, like the budgets: a cap of 250.00 USD comes back as 250.0, not 25000. For a currency with no minor unit, such as JPY, the number is unchanged.
changes.why_better: A campaign spend cap read 100 times too large could be mistaken for a much higher limit. update_campaign takes spend_cap and reports its previous value in major units, so reads and writes now use the same scale.
changes.migration: If you divided spend_cap by 100 (or by the currency's minor-unit factor) yourself, stop: use the value as returned.

changes.what_changed: spend_cap, when named in fields, is now returned in major units of the account currency, like the budgets: a cap of 250.00 USD comes back as 250.0, not 25000. For a currency with no minor unit, such as JPY, the number is unchanged.
changes.why_better: A campaign spend cap read 100 times too large could be mistaken for a much higher limit. get_campaign and update_campaign show spend_cap in major units too, so every tool uses the same scale.
changes.migration: If you divided spend_cap by 100 (or by the currency's minor-unit factor) yourself, stop: use the value as returned.

changes.what_changed: daily_spend_cap, lifetime_spend_cap, daily_min_spend_target and lifetime_min_spend_target, when named in fields, are now returned in major units of the account currency, like the budgets and bids: a cap of 250.00 USD comes back as 250.0, not 25000. For a currency with no minor unit, such as JPY, the numbers are unchanged.
changes.why_better: A cap or minimum spend read 100 times too large could be mistaken for a much higher amount, next to budgets and bids that were already in major units. update_adset takes these four in major units and reports their previous values in major units, so reads and writes now use the same scale.
changes.migration: If you divided these four fields by 100 (or by the currency's minor-unit factor) yourself, stop: use the values as returned.

changes.what_changed: An id that Meta defines as a number must now be digits, and an ad account id digits or act_ followed by digits; anything else is refused before the tool starts. This covers every parameter named campaign_id, adset_id, ad_id, creative_id, audience_id, origin_audience_id, pixel_id, dataset_id, event_source_id, business_id, catalog_id, product_set_id, feed_id, page_id, instagram_account_id, instagram_media_id, study_id, video_id, system_user_id, app_id and account_id, object_id (an ad account, campaign, ad set or ad), and each entry of campaign_ids, ad_ids, object_ids, video_ids, primary_feed_ids and search_page_ids. get_account_pages still takes 'me' as account_id. Spaces around an id and a blank optional id are treated as before. The message names the parameter and what a valid id looks like, and never repeats the value. Each of these parameters' input schemas now carries the pattern. Before, only an id holding a slash, ?, #, .. or a space was refused, and a name or a placeholder such as 'my campaign' or '<campaign_id>' was sent to Meta. Image hashes, Page post and comment ids (digits_digits), paging cursors, export_id, report_run_id, retailer and product ids, interest ids and the other ids listed in meta_ads_mcp/id_formats.py are unchanged.
changes.why_better: A name or a placeholder in an id field no longer spends a rate-limited request and comes back as an unclear error from Meta. The caller is told at once which parameter is wrong and what it should hold, and private text pasted into an id field by mistake is never echoed back or sent to Meta.
changes.migration: Pass the numeric id Meta gave the object, as a string, for example '1234567890', and an ad account as '1234567890' or 'act_1234567890'. Find ids with the list_ and search tools, not by name. An id sent as a JSON number was refused before and still is: send it as a string.

changes.what_changed: bid_amount now refuse true and false before the tool starts, with a message that names the parameter. Before, MCP validation read true as 1 and false as 0, so true was sent to Meta as an amount of 1. Numbers and numeric text are accepted exactly as before, and the input schema is unchanged.
changes.why_better: A budget or bid of true is no longer sent to Meta as 1 (a budget of 1.00 in the account currency, or a 1.00 bid), and false no longer reaches the tool as 0. The caller is told which parameter is wrong instead of a change going through with an amount nobody chose.
changes.migration: Send the amount as a number in major units of the account currency, for example 12.50. Numeric text such as '12.50' still works.

changes.why_better: A budget or bid of true is no longer sent to Meta as 1 (a budget of 1.00 in the account currency, or a 1.00 bid), and false no longer reaches the tool as 0. The caller is told which parameter is wrong instead of a change going through with an amount nobody chose.
changes.migration: Send the amount as a number in major units of the account currency, for example 12.50. Numeric text such as '12.50' still works.

Numbers and numeric text are accepted exactly as before, and the input schema is unchanged.
changes.why_better: A lookalike ratio of true is no longer sent to Meta as a ratio of 1, and false no longer reaches the tool as 0. The caller is told which parameter is wrong instead of an audience being built from a size nobody chose.
changes.migration: Send the ratio as a number, for example 0.01 for the closest 1 percent. Numeric text such as '0.01' still works.

changes.what_changed: retention_days now refuses true and false before the tool starts, with a message that names the parameter. Before, MCP validation read true as 1 and false as 0, so retention_days=true kept people in the audience for one day. Whole numbers and digit text are accepted exactly as before, and the input schema is unchanged.
changes.why_better: A retention period of true is no longer sent to Meta as one day, so people are not dropped from the audience after a day nobody chose. The caller is told which parameter is wrong.
changes.migration: Send the number of days as a whole number, for example 30. Digit text such as '30' still works.

changes.what_changed: A web address that carries a username or password (https://user:pass@host/...) anywhere in image_url is now refused before any request is sent, with a message that names the parameter and never repeats the address. Before, it was sent to Meta as written. Addresses without a login, including ones with an @ in the path or query, are sent exactly as before.
changes.why_better: A URL given to Meta is stored on the ad object and shown in responses, previews, dry runs and errors, so a login in it would be shown to everyone who can read the object. The tools added with the parity work already refused such URLs; these four now do the same.
changes.migration: Host the file or page at an address that needs no login, and pass that address. URLs without a login need no change.

changes.what_changed: An existing creative named inside creative, as creative={'creative_id': ...} or creative={'id': ...}, must now be digits, the same as the top-level creative_id; anything else is refused before the tool starts, with a message that names creative.creative_id or creative.id and never repeats the value. Before, the top-level creative_id was checked but the same id given inside creative was sent to Meta as written. Spaces around the id and a blank value are treated as before.
changes.why_better: All three ways of naming the creative get the same check, so a name or a placeholder given as the nested creative id no longer spends a rate-limited request and comes back as an unclear error from Meta, and private text pasted there is never echoed back or sent to Meta.
changes.migration: Pass the creative's numeric id as a string, for example creative={'creative_id': '1234567890'}, or use the top-level creative_id. Numeric ids need no change.
